suggested_experiment_name: Tokyo-Dish (Hidden Photon Dark Matter Search with Dish Antenna)
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter χ (dimensionless), canonical dark photon coupling
notes: First experimental search for hidden photon CDM using a dish antenna technique. The paper reports a single measured exclusion limit at mγ′ = 3.1 ± 1.2 eV with χ < 6 × 10^-12 at 95% CL. The limit is derived from a null result (Nfit = (−1.9 ± 3.8) × 10^-3 Hz) after background subtraction. The experiment assumes DM is dominated by hidden photons with isotropic velocity distribution (isothermal model) and unpolarized HPs. Local DM density ρCDM,halo = 0.3 GeV/cm³ is used in the sensitivity calculation per equation (1.1). The coupling type is unambiguously DarkPhoton (kinetic mixing χ), and the numerical limit is clearly stated in the abstract and Figure 5. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.75, 47)) | Vision: Figure 5 shows the exclusion region (χ-m_γ' parameter space) for hidden photon dark matter. The red solid curve labeled 'Result' traces the Tokyo-Dish experiment's constraint boundary. The region ABOVE this curve is excluded (higher coupling values ruled out). The plot includes multiple other constraints: CMB (gray), Coulomb (yellow), LSW (light blue), CAST (orange), Solar lifetime (teal), and HP CDDM allowed region (light reddish-brown). The 'Haloscope' region marks previous axion DM results translated assuming HP composition. The boundary shows a relatively flat response at low masses (~1e-12 to 1e-6 eV) with coupling ~1e-5, then gradually decreases toward higher masses. The curve exhibits a characteristic shape with a shallow minimum around 1e-4 to 1e-2 eV before rising again at very high masses. Axis ranges confirmed: x ∈ [1e-12, 1e6] eV, y ∈ [1e-16, 1e-5] (dimensionless χ). | Calibration: No calibration needed
